title: Branding by @aliszu: Visual content drives 94% more engagement than text-only formats. Rese
notes:
Visual content drives 94% more engagement than text-only formats. Research shows that combining text with visuals boosts retention by 65%. So I thought: how can I use that knowledge? My goal was to make webarc[.]day playful and fun to read. But as we're sharing news, I wanted to avoid brand characters and build emotions with color instead. Categories by Color: Green - Development & Infrastructure Associated with balance and progress. Makes technical information feel approachable rather than overwhelming. Pink - Design & Frontend Breaks tech industry stereotypes. Signals that innovation doesn't have to feel corporate. Yellow - Business & Innovation Captures focus instantly. Perfect for highlighting emerging trends and opportunities. Purple - AI & Programming Conveys sophistication without feeling cold. Ideal for cutting-edge tech topics. What This Means for Readers Brain recognizes patterns before you consciously read anything. After seeing a category color a few times, you start automatically associating topics with their colors. This makes finding what you care about effortless. Technical information is less overwhelming when visually organized. Colors create structure, helping you absorb what you read. And honestly? It's just more enjoyable. What This Means for the Business? The color system aids navigation, helping readers find what they want and stay longer. It's about reducing friction. And there's something to building a brand that people actually enjoy interacting with, not just tolerate!

Designer: @aliszu. Curated on Collect UI (https://collectui.com).
